summary: Kenya abolished visas in January 2024 but replaced them with a mandatory Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) that almost all non-African visitors must obtain at etakenya.go.ke before departure (about 32–34 USD, stays up to 90 days); citizens of most African countries, including South Africa, are exempt from the eTA entirely.

fee.notes: Around 32–34 USD including card processing fees. Every traveler needs one, including children (infants under specific ages may be exempt. Check the portal).

source.name: Republic of Kenya eTA — Official Portal

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on the date of arrival in Kenya.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required if you arrive from, or transited more than 12 hours through, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. Kenya itself has areas of yellow fever risk, so vaccination is also generally recommended for visitors.

vaccinations.name: Malaria prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: Malaria is present in most of Kenya below 2,500 m, including the coast and the main safari parks (Nairobi city is lower-risk). Antimalarial tablets, repellent and bed nets are strongly recommended — talk to a travel clinic before your trip.

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not an entry requirement, but medical coverage including evacuation is strongly recommended — safari areas are remote and serious cases are flown to Nairobi.

onwardTicket.text: The eTA application asks for your flight itinerary and accommodation details, and immigration officers may ask for proof of onward or return travel.

proofOfFunds.text: There is no published fixed amount, but immigration officers may ask travelers to show sufficient means of support for the intended stay.

currencyLimits.text: Cash of 10,000 USD or more (or equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure.

notes: Plastic carrier bags are banned in Kenya — bringing one into the country (even a duty-free or zip-lock bag in your luggage) is an offense with heavy fines. Pack with cloth or paper bags.
Duty-free allowance: 200 cigarettes and 1 liter of spirits per adult.

payments.text: Kenya is a mobile-money country: M-Pesa dominates daily payments everywhere, from market stalls to taxis. Cards work in Nairobi and Mombasa hotels, malls and lodges; carry some shilling cash for small purchases and rural areas, or set up M-Pesa with a local SIM.

safety.text: Safari circuits, lodges and the main tourist areas are generally well run and safe with sensible precautions. Petty crime is common in Nairobi and Mombasa (avoid walking at night, use registered taxis or apps), and areas near the Somali border and parts of the north should be avoided.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Kenya travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: July to October is the dry season and peak safari time — the Great Migration crosses the Maasai Mara roughly July to October. January to February is a second dry window, good for wildlife and the coast.

idp.text: Kenya is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Kenya is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Kenya yet.

tips.text: Apply for the Kenya eTA only at the official portal etakenya.go.ke — search results are full of look-alike sites charging double or triple the official 32–34 USD fee.
Plastic carrier bags are illegal in Kenya — even one packed in your suitcase can mean a fine at the airport. Use cloth or paper bags for laundry and shoes.

National park fees are charged per person per day in USD (the Maasai Mara is around 100–200 USD per adult per day in high season) and are usually not included in quoted safari prices. Check what your package covers and carry a card for park gates.
M-Pesa mobile money is how Kenya pays for almost everything. A local SIM with M-Pesa set up makes taxis, markets and tips far easier than cash or cards.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Kenya?
faq.answer: Kenya no longer issues tourist visas, but US citizens — like almost all non-African visitors — must obtain an Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) at etakenya.go.ke before departure. It costs about 32–34 USD, is usually approved within 3 business days, and allows stays of up to 90 days.

faq.question: Is the Kenya eTA the same as a visa?
faq.answer: Functionally it replaced the old 50 USD eVisa in January 2024: it is a pre-travel authorization that every non-exempt visitor needs, costs about 32–34 USD, and is applied for online at etakenya.go.ke. Citizens of most African countries and East African Community members are exempt.

faq.question: How early should I apply for the Kenya eTA?
faq.answer: The official processing standard is up to 3 business days, and Kenya recommends applying at least two weeks before travel. Applications from some nationalities undergo extra vetting and can take longer, so do not leave it to the last minute — airlines check the eTA at check-in.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Kenya?
faq.answer: It is mandatory only if you arrive from or transited through a yellow fever risk country (much of Africa and South America). However, Kenya itself has yellow fever risk areas, so the vaccination is recommended for most visitors, and having the certificate avoids questions when you travel onward in the region.

faq.question: When is the best time for a Kenya safari?
faq.answer: July to October, during the dry season, when the Great Migration is in the Maasai Mara and animals concentrate around water. January to February is a quieter dry-season alternative. Book park lodges months ahead for the migration window and budget for daily park fees on top of your safari price.
